0.2.0.lead: Notifications now reach the phone without an extra app: nexsift installs as an app and sends straight to the device.

sections.title: This device as a target
sections.body: Open nexsift over https on the phone, add it to the home screen as an app and sign the device up there. Each device signs itself up once and then has its own minimum level and quiet hours. A tap on a notification opens the line.
sections.where: Rules › Forwarding to the phone › + Target › This device

sections.title: Encrypted all the way to the device
sections.body: Every message is encrypted for the single device. The push service of Google, Apple or Mozilla only sees that something arrives.

small: If a device signs off or the app is removed, its target switches itself off and says why.

0.3.0.lead: Tidied up: settings in tabs, a page of its own for "About nexsift", and from now on this window after every update.

sections.title: Settings in tabs
sections.body: Account, sign-in, addresses, retention and languages each have a tab of their own instead of one long page.

sections.title: About nexsift
sections.body: Version, license, links to the source and every "What's new" so far are on a page of their own. This window can be opened again from there.

sections.title: Several devices, and signing off
sections.body: Every device you sign up is a target of its own. In the list, the device in your hand says "this device". Any device can sign any device off, a lost phone from the computer for instance. The same device signing up twice stays one target.
sections.where: Rules › Forwarding to the phone › tap the device › Sign device off

small: Signing a device up is now one step that saves right away.
If the browser refuses the sign-up, its own reason is shown.
Help texts at the edge of the page are no longer cut off.

0.4.0.lead: Signing in through authentik is now bound to your account there, and you make the connection yourself.

sections.title: Link with authentik
sections.body: Under Sign-in there is "Your account at authentik". One click on "Link with authentik now", sign in there once, done. From then on nexsift lets exactly this authentik account in and no other. The link is removed in the same place.
sections.where: Settings › Sign-in › Your account at authentik

sections.title: No more matching by email address
sections.body: Until now the same email address counted as proof on the first sign-in. Since authentik reports every address as verified for nexsift, that was too weak. If you are linked already, nothing changes; otherwise link once. The address field under Account is gone for that reason.

small: Signing in with a password can only be switched off once authentik is linked, and the link only removed while the password counts again. That way you cannot lock yourself out.

0.5.0.lead: nexsift now backs itself up, keeps a log you read in the interface, and lets dashboards like nexdeck read along.

sections.title: Backup and restore
sections.body: A copy of the database every night, plus one before every update that changes the database. Download gives you an encrypted ZIP with the key, which 7-Zip opens too. Only such an archive on another device is a real backup. Restoring first shows what the archive holds and makes a copy of the current state.

sections.title: The log in the interface
sections.body: The newest lines with a filter by level, search, download and clear. To track down a problem, switch to Detailed or Trace; both go back by themselves after the chosen time. Every error message now names a request id; type it into the search and you see exactly that request. Tokens, topics and credentials are on no level.

sections.title: API keys for dashboards
sections.body: Flip the switch first, then make one key per dashboard. It reads only numbers and titles under /api/v1/status and /api/v1/threads, no message text, and changes nothing.

small: The log is a file at data/logs/nexsift.log and tidies itself up.
NEXSIFT_LOG_LEVEL is no longer needed. When set it overrides the level from the interface, as an emergency exit.

0.6.0.lead: Pushover is a target of its own now, next to ntfy, Gotify and Telegram.

sections.title: Pushover
sections.body: Create an application on pushover.net, enter its API token and your user key, done. Critical messages arrive with high priority and sound through the quiet hours set in the Pushover app, warnings arrive normally, info without a sound. The all-clear comes with a normal sound. If the message carries a link, it comes along.
sections.where: Rules › Forwarding to the phone › + Target › Pushover

small: When Pushover refuses a push, the target says why, for instance that the token is wrong.

0.7.0.lead: Open problems can now be closed by hand, Uptime Kuma says in plain words what is wrong, and a lot works with a right click and for several messages at once.

sections.title: Done, even without an all-clear
sections.body: Some senders never say "back again", such as Synology about a stopped container. You close such problems yourself now: open the message and tap Done. In Critical open one button closes them all, only those of the chosen source if one is selected. If the same problem comes back, it is a new message.
sections.where: Inbox › message › Done, or Critical open › All done

sections.title: Uptime Kuma in plain words
sections.body: Instead of "MeTube is down" and "connect ECONNREFUSED" it now says "MeTube is not reachable", with the group, the address and the likely cause below: not running, not answering, unknown name, expired certificate and more. Missing signs of life from push checks and expiring certificates are messages of their own, groups only a note. Kuma's own sentence is still under raw data.

sections.title: Right click
sections.body: A right click on a message shows everything you can do with it: mark it done, archive, read, mute the source, delete. On a source on the left it is about all of its messages, on Critical open about every open problem.
sections.where: Inbox › right click on a message, a source or a view

sections.title: Several at once
sections.body: Ctrl and click adds single messages, Shift and click a range, Ctrl+A all of them. Or click the mark on the left of a line; on a phone a tap is enough. The top then says how many are selected, and Done, Archive, Read and Delete act on all of them.
sections.where: Inbox › mark on the left of a line

sections.title: Language of pushes
sections.body: What nexsift words itself reaches the phone in the language you choose here. English out of the box. What a sender writes itself stays as it came.

small: New keys: r marks done, x selects, Shift+F10 opens the menu. The overview comes with ?.
A push to ntfy with an umlaut in its title got lost. Fixed.

0.7.1.lead: Tidy up whole views and sources at once, with a right click.

sections.title: Archive, bring back, delete everything
sections.body: A right click on Inbox, Unread or Critical open archives everything there. On Archive you bring everything back or empty it. On a source you archive or delete all of its messages, those in the archive too. Deleting asks first and names how many, and everything can be undone.
sections.where: Inbox › right click on a view or a source

small: The actions cover the whole view, not only the lines loaded.

0.7.2.lead: What you open in Unread stays there until you move on.

sections.title: Messages no longer vanish while you read them
sections.body: Opening a message in Unread marks it read, and it then dropped out of the list while you were still reading. Now it stays, without the blue dot, and the number in the side bar still counts down. Once you change the view, the source or the search, it is gone from Unread.

small: The same holds when you mark it read yourself with u or the button.

0.7.3.lead: The authentik button now copes with a second nexsift at the same authentik.

sections.title: A second nexsift at the same authentik
sections.body: If another nexsift is already connected to your authentik, the button now creates a provider and an application of its own, with this instance's address in the name, such as “nexsift (nexsift.example.com)”. Until now it took over the existing ones and sent the first instance's sign-in here, which broke it. Running the button again on the same instance still updates what is there.

small: The setup steps no longer name a fixed provider and application, since they can now carry other names.
